intro: Professionals and everyday users convert gigabytes (GB) to megabytes (MB) when working across metric and metric standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One gigabyte (decimal) equals 1,000 megabytes, while 1 megabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 gigabytes. Whether you are verifying digital storage specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many megabytes (MB) are in 1 gigabyte (decimal) (GB)?
faqs.answer: There are 1,000 megabytes (MB) in 1 gigabyte (decimal) (GB), which rounds to 1,000 MB for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 megabyte (decimal) equals 0.001 gigabytes.

faqs.question: How do I convert gigabytes to megabytes (GB to MB)?
faqs.answer: To convert gigabytes to megabytes, use the formula: MB = GB × 1,000. For example, converting 16 GB gives 16,000 MB.

faqs.question: What is 16 gigabytes in megabytes?
faqs.answer: 16 gigabytes (GB) equals exactly 16,000 megabytes (MB) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
